correctness.rationale: For the incidence bipartite graph S(K_n), fort membership is equivalent to delta(X) subset Y and deg_Y(w)!=1 for each unselected original w. If X is empty, inclusion-minimality reduces exactly to simple cycles. If |X|=1, removing the original vertex leaves a proper fort. For |X|>=2, extra selected subdivision vertices outside the cut are removable; both cut sides of size >=2 contain a cycle fort, leaving only the all-original set and n exceptional star-complement sets. These are proved inclusion-minimal against every proper subset. Their size counts give the claimed polynomial and unbounded gap. An independent full-subset enumerator checked the claim for n=3..6 (2,131,004 subsets). No finite experiment is represented as an unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: The minimal-fort hypergraph is the exact family of zero-forcing obstructions, rather than merely a number. Its complete classification for the canonical once-subdivided complete graph distinguishes cycle-generated minimal obstructions from large original-vertex star complements. The exact polynomial has a growing forbidden cardinality interval and factorial total count. These facts permit direct fort-cover and transversal investigations and are not a routine consequence of the already known scalar zero-forcing number. The objects and sizes are natural, not arbitrary slices.
